name: Saugus
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Saugus, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Saugus, MA: the Town Hall tree lighting with Santa, a petting zoo and sleigh rides, plus Santa by the fire at Breakheart Reservation.
lede: Saugus does Christmas in one big night at Town Hall, when Santa arrives at 7 pm sharp to switch on the lights, plus a quieter visit with Santa by the fire at Breakheart Reservation.
celebrates: The Town of Saugus holds its annual Tree Lighting outside Saugus Town Hall on Central Street, planned by the Youth and Recreation Department, the Department of Public Works and Building Maintenance. Families ride a trackless train, visit a petting zoo, take horse-drawn sleigh rides and line up for photos with winter characters, and the town serves complimentary cookies, hot cocoa and cider. At 7 pm sharp Santa arrives and lights the trees on the Town Hall grounds and the Saugus Center rotary. A gingerbread house contest fills the Town Hall auditorium, Congregation Ahavas Sholom lights a menorah outside Town Hall, and the Friends of Breakheart host Santa at the reservation.
lastyear: In 2025 the Tree Lighting Ceremony was held on Friday, December 5, from 5 to 8:30 pm outside Saugus Town Hall, with a trackless train, a petting zoo, sleigh rides, a bounce house and photos with winter characters. Itemlive reported that Town Manager Scott Crabtree welcomed families on a cold night, Santa and his sleigh arrived at 7 pm guided by a horse, the Saugus High School band played, and the trees around Town Hall and Saugus Center lit up as the switch was flipped.
facts: Saugus is home to the Saugus Iron Works National Historic Site, which the National Park Service describes as the first successful iron works in America, in operation from about 1646 to 1670. Breakheart Reservation, where the Friends of Breakheart host Santa, began as a private hunting reserve around a lodge that Ben Johnson and two friends opened in 1891, and the state now manages more than 600 acres of forest there. At the Town Hall lighting, Santa switches on lights strung across the trees and the Saugus Center rotary.
trains: The MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line does not stop in Saugus. Neighboring Lynn has two stations on the line, River Works and Lynn Interim, with trains to North Station in Boston. For a holiday train, Edaville in Carver runs its Holiday Express through Christmas lights and has Santa meet-and-greets. In Lowell, the National Streetcar Museum has hands-on streetcar exhibits for kids, and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society shows off steam locomotive No. 410 on Dutton Street.

kidfact: Saugus had one of the very first iron works in America. Workers there made iron from about 1646 to 1670, which is almost 380 years ago.
faq: What happens at the Saugus tree lighting?

The town sets up a trackless train, a petting zoo, horse-drawn sleigh rides, bounce houses, a mechanical surf machine, photos with winter characters and a photo booth outside Town Hall, along with free cookies, hot cocoa and cider. At 7 pm sharp Santa arrives and turns on the lights on the Town Hall grounds and the Saugus Center rotary.
Who organizes the Saugus tree lighting?

The Town of Saugus, through the Town Manager's office. The Youth and Recreation Department, the Department of Public Works, the Building Maintenance Department and other town employees plan and set up the event, and the town thanks volunteers and local businesses for their help each year. Questions about the gingerbread contest go to 781-231-4118.
Where can kids see Santa in Saugus besides Town Hall?

The Friends of Breakheart Reservation and the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation host Santa at the Christopher P. Dunne Visitor Center at 177 Forest Street. Families bring their own camera for photos, and there are candy canes, holiday crafts and light refreshments. DCR offers free parking at the Forest Street entrance.
What is the Saugus Iron Works?

It is a National Historic Site in Saugus that preserves what the National Park Service calls the first successful iron works in America, which operated from about 1646 to 1670. Today the National Park Service preserves the site and tells the story of the colonial ironworkers who made iron there.
How do I get to Saugus by train?

Saugus has no Commuter Rail stop. Take the MBTA Newburyport/Rockport Line from North Station in Boston to River Works or Lynn Interim in neighboring Lynn, then continue by bus, taxi or car. The MBTA posts a fall and winter schedule for the line, so check train times before you go.
